name: the coercion pass never runs
why: The original org/config-handling.org F2 defect, reverted wholesale: without the call, numeric settings stay exactly as VZ_MBLibrary stored them. Both the mechanism assertions and the user-visible collapse assertion must notice, so this is the entry that proves the spec is testing the fix rather than something adjacent.
grep: a numeric string is coerced to a Number

name: coercion runs AFTER the settings copy instead of before
why: Placement guard. `settings` is a shallow copy, not a reference, so coercing after Object.assign leaves the copy holding strings. Only ONE read consumes that copy today (the debug-logging callback, a checkbox), so this is expected to PASS — recorded so the next person to move the call knows the ordering is deliberate and currently unpinned, rather than discovering it by breaking something subtle later.
grep: a numeric string is coerced to a Number

name: an empty string becomes 0 instead of the schema default
why: Number('') === 0, so this is the natural way to write the coercion and it is wrong: a cleared number field would silently mean the documented '0 to disable'. Only the empty-string test may notice — if the '0' or 'abc' tests fail too, the fallback branch is being reached for inputs that should parse.
grep: an empty string falls back to the schema default

name: an unparseable value is written through as NaN
why: Drops the fallback to cfg.default. The 'unparseable' test must notice, and so must the whole-schema sweep, which asserts no setting is left NaN — that second failure is the point of having the sweep at all.
grep: an unparseable value falls back to the schema default

name: already-valid numbers are re-coerced instead of skipped
why: Efficiency guard only. Removing the early-out makes every number take the String()/Number() round trip, which produces the identical value — so this is expected to PASS. Recorded rather than left unmentioned: the skip exists so an untouched profile costs nothing, not for correctness.
grep: a NUMBER threshold still behaves exactly as before

name: absent keys get the schema default written in
why: The VZ_MBLibrary-failed-to-load stub path has Lib.settings === {}, where each consumer's own `?? default` must apply. No fixture exercises that path — the library always loads — so this is expected to PASS. Recorded so the guard's reason survives: removing it would change stub behaviour with nothing to catch it.
grep: every numeric setting ends up a real Number

name: sa_render_threshold back to || 5000
why: The falsy-zero defect, restored. Expected to PASS, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: `||` and `??` only differ when the value is 0 AND the row count exceeds the hardcoded fallback of 5000. Every fixture in this suite renders 12 rows, so both operators take the same branch. Pinning it needs a >5000-row fixture, which costs a multi-minute fetch for one boolean. The change is still required — the coercion makes the stored '0' falsy, where before it was the truthy string '0' that survived `||` and then failed `> 0`, i.e. it worked by accident.
grep: a numeric string is coerced to a Number

name: sa_chunked_render_threshold back to || 1000 in both renderers
why: As above, with a fallback of 1000 against 12 rendered rows. Both call sites are mutated together deliberately: they are the same guarantee in the two table modes, and a spec that could see one would see the other.
